title: Internal categories tab lists its columns and General Internal as default
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The page has two tabs, Internal categories and No Charge categories.
  • The Internal categories tab shows the columns Category, QuickBooks expense account (with the green QuickBooks mark), Internal customers using it, and Work orders.
  • General Internal is listed with a "Default" badge.
  • Each row has a menu with Edit and Archive.
  • The buttons "New Internal Category" and "New No Charge Category" show.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S1-R13: “Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders is a page with two tabs. Internal categories: columns Category (the default carries a Default badge), QuickBooks expense account (with the QuickBooks mark; "Not set" with a warning icon when empty), Internal customers using it, Work orders (count, all time; a billable work order with a no-charge line of the category counts too), and a row menu with Edit and Archive. No Charge categories: Category, QuickBooks expense account, Original work order (Required / Not asked), Work orders, row menu. Buttons "New Internal Category" and "New No Charge Category". The starting set is seeded for every organization when this release ships, so the categories, the QuickBooks rows (S5-R5) and the hub rows (S6-R2) exist before the setting is turned on; turning the setting on seeds nothing: General Internal (default, cannot be archived); Warranty (requires the original work order), Goodwill (does not), Comeback (requires). Archived categories stay on the work orders and lines that used them and in the report filter under Archived; a "Show archived (n)" link lists them with Restore. The page needs 'Settings — Service', like every Administration > Service page; while the setting is off it shows the notice "Internal Work Orders is off. Turn it on in Settings > Work Orders." and the lists stay editable. Each list holds up to 100 active categories; past that, the New button is disabled with "You can have up to 100 active categories in this list. Archive one to add another." The QuickBooks expense account column is shown only while the current location is connected to QuickBooks.”
  • S1-R16: “A category has a stable key; renaming it keeps the history, the report filter and the mappings. Archiving a category in use keeps it on existing work orders, lines, documents and reports; it is no longer offered in any select. The default Internal category cannot be archived; changing the default moves nothing on existing customers. The green QuickBooks mark (the existing QuickBooks icon) is shown wherever a field maps to QuickBooks: the account columns and pickers of S1-R13 and S1-R14, the asset field of S1-R15 and the Settings hint of S1-R3. Archiving a category that is the stored default of customers or assets first shows "[n] internal customers and [m] assets use this category as their default. Their new work orders will use the next category in line." The stored value stays on the customer and the asset, shown as "[name] (archived)" with the hint "Archived. Pick an active category."; resolution for a new work order (S2-R1) skips archived categories: the asset's, else the customer's, else the default Internal category, the first active one wins. Restore puts everything back as it was.”
  • Terminology: “Category → a shop-managed entry in one of two lists on Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders: Internal categories (where the cost of work on the shop's own equipment goes) and No Charge categories (why a customer's work order or line is free). Each carries a QuickBooks expense account per location and, on No Charge, whether it requires the original work order. Replaces "reason".”
  • Key Decisions: “Categories are shop-managed and carry the account; the work order never asks an accounting question. The category of an internal work order is resolved from the asset, else the customer, else General Internal; a no-charge category is picked where No Charge is set.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
